 Advertisement Election investigation underway in Georgia after 388 late votes flip House lead
 Advertisement Updated: 11:38 AM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Graham Cawthon Digital Media Manager Election investigation underway in Georgia after 388 late votes flip House lead
 Updated: 11:38 AM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Graham Cawthon Digital Media Manager SEMINOLE COUNTY, Ga. — Above video: Your Monday headlines 
 Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger has opened an investigation after hundreds of Election Day votes were reported late in Seminole County , changing the unofficial leader in a state House race.
 Advertisement The additional results put Republican incumbent Rep. Gerald Greene ahead of Democrat Harry James in southwest Georgia’s House District 154. If Greene’s lead holds, it would narrow Democrats’ expected majority in the Georgia House.
 Before the results were added, Greene trailed James by fewer than 100 votes. Raffensperger’s office initially reported that Greene had taken a 262-vote lead. Unofficial state results updated Saturday showed Greene with 10,193 votes to James’ 9,932 — a margin of 261 votes.
 Democrats poised to seize Georgia House for first time in more than 20 years County disputes missing-card account
 The discrepancy surfaced during the state’s post-election review, when officials found about 388 more voters recorded as having checked in at Seminole County polling places on Election Day than the number of ballots reported as cast.
 Raffensperger’s office said results from a memory card had not been properly uploaded into the county’s election management system.
 Seminole County Elections Supervisor Ron Foskey disputed reports that a card was missing or newly discovered. He said all cards were accounted for on election night, but the final step to validate and publish results from the last precinct’s card had not been completed. County officials completed that step Friday, he said.
 “Georgia’s election safeguards are designed to identify discrepancies, and that is exactly what these guardrails did,” Raffensperger said in a statement.
 “This oversight didn’t just affect the numbers — it changed who was leading an election. That is unacceptable, and we intend to find out exactly how it happened.”
 The investigation will examine whether required procedures were followed and what changes may be needed to prevent similar problems.
 Stephanie Burgess flips Georgia House District 164, says voters 'didn't feel heard' A narrow expected majority
 Democrats remain on track to control the 180-member Georgia House, but Greene’s lead could leave them with a slim margin.
 If his lead and other apparent results hold, Democrats are projected to have 92 seats — one more than the 91 needed for a majority. That would leave party leaders with little room for defections or absences on close votes.
 The final margin could also depend on a Dec. 1 runoff in House District 151. Republican Rep. Mike Cheokas faces Democrat Ethan Wolfe after neither won a majority in a three-way contest.
